source1: W.D.E. Coulson, D.C. Haggis, M.S. Mook & J.L. Tobin, Excavations on the Kastro at Kavousi: An Architectural Overview, Hesperia 66.3, ASCSA/1997 - https://www.ascsa.edu.gr/uploads/media/hesperia/148394.pdf
source2: University of Cincinnati (A. Kotsonas, Knossos Urban Landscape Project), Archaeological Discovery Yields Surprising Revelations about Europe's Oldest City, University of Cincinnati/2016 - https://www.uc.edu/news/articles/legacy/enews/2016/01/archaeological-discovery-yields-surprising-revelations-about-europes-oldest-city.html
notes: Archaeological phase (LM IIIC-Subminoan), no recorded central authority. Kavousi Kastro inhabited continuously LM IIIC to 7th century; Knossos recovered after c.1200 BCE and grew in Early Iron Age. Settlement and material continuity into Geometric Crete.

successor: Tsardom of Russia (Yakutsk fort and voevodstvo)
source1: Marjorie Mandelstam Balzer, Yakut, Encyclopedia of World Cultures, Gale (via Encyclopedia.com) - https://www.encyclopedia.com/humanities/encyclopedias-almanacs-transcripts-and-maps/yakut
source2: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Yakutsk, Encyclopaedia Britannica - https://www.britannica.com/place/Yakutsk
notes: Sakha were autonomous lineage and territorial groups under toyon councils, no paramount state. Russian fort on Lena 1632; Tygyn-led revolts failed; Lena valley under tsarist tribute by 1642. Q3 Y nominal only, no central authority existed.

source1: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Liao dynasty, Encyclopaedia Britannica - https://www.britannica.com/topic/Liao-dynasty?oasmId=121
source2: Silk Road Seattle, University of Washington, The Khitan and the Liao Dynasty (based on A.T. Kessler, Empires Beyond the Great Wall, 1993) - https://www.depts.washington.edu/silkroad/exhibit/khitans/essay.html
notes: Jurchen, conquered Liao subjects/tributaries, revolted 1114, founded Jin 1115, took Liao capitals, ended Liao 1125. Brief counts rebellious tributaries as internal, so T1a not T2 (contestable). Uprisings increased beforehand. Orkhon/'Early Mongols' entries mismatch core.

successor: British Empire (Gold Coast Colony; Ashanti crown colony from 1902)
source1: African Studies Centre Leiden Library, Asante Kingdom (web dossier), Leiden University/2002, updated 2024 - https://www.ascleiden.nl/content/webdossiers/asante-kingdom
source2: SOAS Library, Scrapbook on the Ashanti Expedition, 1895-1896 (MS 381226, catalogue description), SOAS University of London - https://library.soas.ac.uk/Collection/MS_381226
notes: British expedition occupied Kumasi January 1896, deposed and exiled Prempeh I; 1900 rising crushed; annexed 1901-02. Civil war 1884-88 followed Mensa Bonsu's 1883 overthrow (Austin, Journal of African History 1996). Database end 1895 slightly early.

source1: Encyclopedia of World Cultures, Jivaro, Gale (via Encyclopedia.com) - https://www.encyclopedia.com/humanities/encyclopedias-almanacs-transcripts-and-maps/jivaro
source2: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Jivaro, Encyclopaedia Britannica - https://www.britannica.com/topic/Jivaro
notes: Shuar communities politically independent, no central authority. 1930s gold-rush fighting ended when Salesians obtained a government reservation (c.1935); incorporation through missions and settlers, Shuar 'never really conquered'. 1931 looks like a dataset convention; weak evidence.

source1: Smithsonian National Museum of the American Indian, Haudenosaunee Guide for Educators, NMAI/2009 - https://americanindian.si.edu/sites/1/files/pdf/education/HaudenosauneeGuide.pdf
source2: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Iroquois Confederacy, Encyclopaedia Britannica - https://www.britannica.com/topic/Iroquois-Confederacy
notes: Grand Council and Onondaga council fire persist today (NMAI 2009); 1848 marks Seneca Nation's constitution deposing hereditary chiefs, not Council's end. Britannica ends Confederacy c.1784; US sovereignty over core predates W, so alternatives exist.

successor: Muslim sultanate of Lakhnauti/Bengal (Rukunuddin Kaikaus, Shamsuddin Firuz Shah)
source1: Banglapedia: National Encyclopedia of Bangladesh, Sonargaon, Asiatic Society of Bangladesh - https://en.banglapedia.org/index.php/Sonargaon
source2: Banglapedia: National Encyclopedia of Bangladesh, Shamsuddin Firuz Shah, Asiatic Society of Bangladesh - https://en.banglapedia.org/index.php/Shamsuddin_Firuz_Shah
notes: Late Deva king Danujamadhava Dasharathadeva (Danuj Rai) ruled Vanga from Sonargaon; independent Hindu rule there ended 1302 as Lakhnauti sultans Kaikaus and Firuz Shah conquered eastern Bengal. Database lists no capital; evidence thin.

successor: Local Late Intermediate Period groups of Ayacucho (Chanka-associated)
source1: Lidio M. Valdez & Cirilo Vivanco, Arqueologia de la Cuenca del Qaracha, Ayacucho, Peru, Latin American Antiquity 5(2), Cambridge University Press/1994 - https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/latin-american-antiquity/article/arqueologia-de-la-cuenca-del-qaracha-ayacucho-peru/516290D1F168BA1CB6DB2212CF30107A
source2: Dumbarton Oaks (Katharina Schreiber), Theorizing the Wari Collapse, Dumbarton Oaks Research Library/2013 - https://www.doaks.org/events/pre-columbian-studies/other/theorizing-the-wari-collapse
notes: Huari and Ayacucho Wari sites abandoned around AD 900-1100 amid political and demographic collapse of unclear cause; fortified hilltop sites and warfare among former Wari elements followed. No documented conquest. Database successor (Cuzco) is another region.

successor: Late Angkor (Khmer kingdom at Angkor, continuing)
source1: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Jayavarman VII, Encyclopaedia Britannica - https://www.britannica.com/biography/Jayavarman-VII
source2: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Zhou Daguan, Encyclopaedia Britannica - https://www.britannica.com/biography/Zhou-Da-guan
notes: Jayavarman VII died c.1220; Angkor still a thriving Khmer capital in 1296, so no break. Preceding crisis: usurpation, 1177 Cham sack of Yasodharapura, rebellions amid constant war (Pash, EBSCO 2019).

source1: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Ikhshidid dynasty, Encyclopaedia Britannica - https://www.britannica.com/print/article/282600
source2: Suzan Yalman, The Fatimid Caliphate (909-1171), Heilbrunn Timeline of Art History, Metropolitan Museum of Art/2001 - https://www.metmuseum.org/toah/hd/fati/hd_fati.htm
notes: Fatimid general Jawhar, from Ifriqiya, conquered Egypt 969, ending Ikhshidid rule under boy ruler Abu al-Fawaris. Kafur's era saw plague, famine, earthquake; his 968 death prompted invasion. Period merges Tulunids, Abbasid interlude, Ikhshidids.
